description: We are building RotaOpt, a free browser tool that uses NASA POWER data to recommend climate-robust crop rotations for the Field Shift challenge.
summary:
RotaOpt is a free browser tool that helps farmers choose better crop rotations using NASA data. We developed it for the Field Shift challenge. It downloads live NASA POWER data (temperature, daily maximum, rainfall, soil wetness) for any field, then combines it with the farmer's soil, available irrigation water and priorities: profit, bad-year protection, water saving and soil health.

RotaOpt searches every feasible rotation with an exact solver and an Artificial Bee Colony optimiser, recommends the best plan, and explains each choice. It stress-tests the plan against every multi-year window of the NASA record and under extra warming. Farmers can lock any season or change prices, so the tool supports their judgment instead of replacing it.

This matters because common rotations such as cotton-wheat drain groundwater and soil while climate shifts. RotaOpt helps farmers use less water, protect soil and reduce risk.
details:
PROBLEM

In irrigated South Asia, cotton-wheat and rice-wheat dominate. They drain groundwater, deplete soil organic matter and are exposed to terminal heat and erratic monsoons. Farmers lack a tool that weighs profit, bad-year risk, irrigation water and soil health together using local climate evidence.

WHAT IT DOES

RotaOpt is a free browser-based decision-support tool for the Field Shift challenge. The user picks a field on a map. The app downloads 21 years of monthly NASA POWER data (2005-2025) for that location. The user enters soil texture, soil health, irrigation water per season, which crops are possible, local prices and four priority weights: profit, bad-year resilience, water saving and soil health. RotaOpt then recommends an optimised crop rotation and explains every choice.

HOW IT WORKS

1. A crop-season model computes relative yield for every crop in every NASA year from temperature suitability, an FAO-33 water-stress response (rainfall, stored soil water, irrigation) and a heat-stress factor.

2. Rotation effects are added: legume nitrogen credit, late-sowing penalty, same-crop repeat penalty and a soil-health index.

3. Four objectives are evaluated over rolling windows of real weather: mean profit, bad-year profit (mean of the worst 20% of windows), irrigation use and end-of-plan soil health.

4. For 3-year plans, all feasible rotations are enumerated, giving the exact optimum and exact Pareto front. For 5-year plans (about 10^8 sequences), a discrete Artificial Bee Colony optimiser finds the plan.

5. The plan is stress-tested with a "Rotation Time Machine" (replay through every observed window), warming and rainfall what-if sliders, and the field's own observed NASA trend extrapolated to 2040.

FARMER IN CONTROL

Any season can be locked to a crop and the optimiser re-plans around it. A swap test shows what each alternative would cost. Crop menu, prices and weights are editable.

RESULT IN OUR PILOT (Multan, Punjab, Pakistan)

[NUMBERS]

VALIDITY AND HONESTY

The Optimiser tab runs live self-checks (ABC versus the exact optimum and versus random search, plus model invariants). NASA POWER (MERRA-2) runs warm over the arid Punjab plains, so we keep NASA's year-to-year variability and trends but remove the regional offset using approximate station normals for Multan. Raw values stay visible in the Diagnostics table and the correction can be switched off. Crop parameters are literature-informed priors (FAO-33, FAO-56, EcoCrop) and are not yet calibrated to district yield statistics, so the tool is meant for comparing rotations, not for forecasting absolute yields.

IMPACT

Less irrigation per hectare, healthier soil and fewer disastrous seasons, with decisions staying in the farmer's hands. The pipeline works anywhere NASA POWER covers once local crop calendars are added.

CREATIVITY

Instead of a single "best crop", RotaOpt optimises across four competing goals, shows the trade-off (Pareto) front, and tests each plan against every year NASA recorded, so farmers see risk, not just averages.

TOOLS

JavaScript (single-file web app, runs fully in the browser), Chart.js, Leaflet with CARTO map tiles, NASA POWER API, GitHub Pages for hosting. Automated tests for the model and the interface.

NEXT STEPS

Validate against yield statistics and farmer trials; add NASA SMAP soil moisture, MODIS/VIIRS NDVI and OpenET/ECOSTRESS evapotranspiration as independent checks; Urdu/Punjabi interface and offline mobile build.

TEAM

Team CASPAM, Multan, Pakistan.
